subject: FinCo migration compatibility & competitive eval - next tests & recap
messages:
From: Evan Morales <evan.morales@finco.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: FinCo discovery: migration compatibility & perf goals

Marissa / Redwood team —

Thanks again for the call today. High-level summary from our side and asks so we can move to a short POC: 

- Why we're evaluating: FinCo needs to reduce per-token inference cost and avoid vendor lock while keeping parity with current OpenAI-based endpoints for our customer-facing chat flows. Latency SLO is < 400ms p50 for 2048-token context in our region.
- Key risk areas: OpenAI-API compatibility, tokenization/response drift, streaming behavior, and compliance (data retention + audit logs).

Requests / next steps we discussed:
1) A short smoke test showing Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint returning identical-ish outputs for our top 30 prompts (we'll provide the prompt set).
2) A comparison run against our hyperscaler incumbent (CloudBig) — perf numbers and costs for identical workload.
3) Info on SDK changes required for a swap (we need a minimal example).

I've attached our migration requirements workbook. Please also include any known differences in default settings (temp, top_p, tokenization) that could explain output diffs.

Goal: agree on a 2-week POC plan and test harness so we can decide if Redwood can meet parity + cost targets.

Thanks,
Evan
Director of Platform Engineering
FinCo

Attachment: finco-migration-requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Morales <evan.morales@finco.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinCo discovery: migration compatibility & perf goals

Evan —

Great to talk — thanks for the clear priorities. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we can get your POC running this week: 

Recap:
- Goals: parity on quality + streaming, <400ms p50 for 2k context in us-west, and predictable unit economics versus CloudBig.
- Risks: tokenization differences, default sampling params, and any model-variant mismatches.

What we'll deliver this sprint (48-72 hrs):
1) A short smoke test harness (OpenAI-compatible endpoint) you can run locally against your prompt set. We include a quick Python + curl example showing SDK swap ("openai" compatible headers).
2) Suggested test plan: perf matrix (p50/p95, throughput), correctness checks (string/QA equality), and prompt-diff harness instructions.
3) A short doc listing default parameter differences and recommended flags to minimize drift (e.g., default temperature, stop token behavior, tokenization mapping).

Immediate asks for your team:
- Share the top 30 prompt set (or confirm the workbook sheet to use).
- Grant test account access: I will create a scoped API key for FinCo's POC (read/write disabled for production stores).

Proposed test schedule:
- Wed: I’ll share the smoke-test repo and instructions.
- Fri: FinCo runs smoke tests and returns logs.
- Following Mon: Redwood runs A/B vs CloudBig and shares perf/cost comparison.

Attachments: redwood-openai-compat-smoke-tests.md, suggested-test-plan.csv
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/finco-redwood-smoke-tests

Cc'ing Logan (infra) to help with any kernel/latency questions. If Dev needs to be looped in for tokenization specifics, we can add him to the thread.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Evan Morales <evan.morales@finco.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCo discovery: migration compatibility & perf goals

Marissa / Redwood —

Thanks, we ran the smoke tests (attached logs). Quick notes:
- Baseline: Our test harness executed your OpenAI-compatible endpoint and CloudBig side-by-side for the 30 prompts.
- Successes: Streaming, most responses aligned in intent. Request/response latency on your endpoint looked good at low qps (p50 ~ 310ms).
- Issues: We observed 4 prompts with notable diffs in tokenization (sometimes missing a leading space) that change the final answer scoring. Two prompts produced shorter completions on Redwood vs CloudBig — seems tied to default max_tokens and stop handling.

Attached: finco-smoke-test-logs.txt (txt)

Questions:
1) Are there explicit tokenization maps or tokenizer versions we should pin to match OpenAI's byte-pair behavior?
2) Is there a quick flag to enforce identical stop-token behavior and max_tokens limits via the OpenAI-compatible wrapper?
3) Timeline: If dialysis passes, what's the lead time for a Dedicated pool in us-west? We may need dedicated capacity for predictable p50 at scale.

Happy to hop on a short call if it's easier — we can do 30 minutes next week.

—Evan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Morales <evan.morales@finco.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCo discovery: migration compatibility & perf goals

Evan —

Thanks for running the first pass and for the detail in the logs. Quick answers and next steps below.

Short answers to your questions:
1) Tokenization: Redwood uses the same BPE tokenizer family for our OpenAI-compatible layer but default byte handling can differ by model variant. Dev — I'll let you add specifics in-thread, but short-term we recommend pinning the tokenizer to "bpe-v1" in the smoke harness. That change should address most leading-space diffs.
2) Stop tokens & max_tokens: Our compatibility wrapper supports explicit params that mirror OpenAI ("stop", "max_tokens", "max_new_tokens"). We've included guidance in the prompt-diff harness to force identical behavior.
3) Dedicated pool lead time: For us-west reserved capacity, typical lead time is ~4–6 weeks after PO; we can provision a temporary Dedicated trial within 5 business days for validation if you sign a short-term commitment.

Proposed tech next steps (this week):
- Dev will drop a small tokenizer patch you can apply to the harness and re-run the 4 failing prompts. (Dev: see TODO inline below).
- We’ll run an A/B perf run at scale (p50/p95/throughput/cost) vs CloudBig and share a side-by-side spreadsheet.
- If results look good, we'll stand up a trial Dedicated pool in us-west for a 2-week performance soak.

Scheduling: Let's book 30 minutes on Mon 2026-03-09 to review re-run results and next steps. I’ll create the HubSpot activity and a Calendly invite.
